title: Compact call manifest: ergonomic JSON-schema, validation pipeline, and human-friendly error envelope
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We need a compact, machine- and human-friendly JSON schema format for tool/function call manifests that is efficient to store in catalog entries, straightforward for model-facing tool descriptions, and robust to runtime validation errors. Current verbose JSON Schema artifacts increase storage/transfer size and produce low-quality runtime error messages that are hard for customers to act on.

Goals: 1) Define a compact schema grammar (subset of JSON Schema + explicit coercion hints) usable in tool manifests; 2) Implement a three-stage validation pipeline (author-time lint, server-side fast validator with best-effort coercion, and strict runtime enforcement option); 3) Design an "error envelope" format that yields actionable, localized, and telemetry-friendly diagnostics (error codes + developer hint + user-facing message + schema path + suggested fixes); 4) Provide compatibility layer to decode older manifest shapes and migrate gracefully.

Proposed compact manifest design (high level):
- Field set: name, description, params (compact schema), examples, stability (stable|experimental), compatibilityAliases (list).
- Compact schema nodes: {"t":"string"}|{"t":"int"}|{"t":"float"}|{"t":"bool"}|{"t":"obj","props":{k:schema}}|{"t":"arr","items":schema}|{"t":"oneof","opts":[schema]} plus optional annotations: "req":true, "min":n, "max":n, "enum":[...], "coerce":"trim|number|bool-from-string".
- Example compact node: {"t":"obj","props":{"email":{"t":"string","req":true,"coerce":"trim"},"age":{"t":"int","min":0}}} 

Validation pipeline details:
1) Author-time lint (CI): static checks that reject obviously invalid manifests, check for deprecated patterns, and emit migration warnings. Confluence design doc + lint rules: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/INF/Compact+Call+Manifest+Design
2) Fast server-side validator: deterministic, zero-dependency C++/Rust implementation used in serving runtime. It implements permissive-coercion rules by default (configurable per route). Known tradeoff: permissive coercion prevents unnecessary customer errors but can mask upstream data problems.
3) Strict runtime enforcement: opt-in per-route flag (enforce_strict=true) that rejects coercion and returns structured error envelope when a mismatch occurs.

Error envelope design (schema for API responses when a call fails validation):
- top-level keys: code (machine code), user_message (short human-friendly text), developer_hint (concise advice + link to schema snippet), path (dot/JSON-pointer path to offending field), expected (compact schema description), actual (stringified incoming value), suggestion (one-line fix suggestion), debug_id (UUID for trace), docs (link to call manifest + examples).
- example response string (for diagnostics): {"code":"CALL_MISSING_REQUIRED","user_message":"Missing required field 'email'.","developer_hint":"email is required and must be a trimmed string; consider adding email or mark as optional. See: https://docs.redwood.ai/...","path":"params.email","expected":"string (trim)","actual":null,"suggestion":"Add 'email' in payload or set 'stability':'experimental' to allow fallback","debug_id":"..."}

Compatibility layer:
- Provide two translation strategies: (A) server-side manifest upgrader that maps legacy JSON Schema fragments to compact manifest nodes using heuristics and migration rules recorded in an internal registry; (B) runtime adapter that accepts old client shapes and translates incoming payloads into canonical shape before validation.
- Record migration warnings in manifest metadata to alert catalog owners.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
- Spec PR merged for compact manifest grammar in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/specs/pull/129 (linked in this ticket).
- Runtime validator implementation merged and exercised with unit tests (C++ target): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842. Benchmark: validation adds <0.2ms median p95 per request for typical 3-field forms.
- Error envelope format adopted by Console and SDKs: example client mapping in SDK repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/418.
- Smoke test: create 3 sample tool manifests (simple, nested, oneof) in catalog, call from hosted API with permissive and strict modes and verify responses and telemetry events.
- Backward-compat: upgrader produces no silent behavior change for >=90% of manifests in catalog; remaining ones flagged and owners notified.

Tradeoffs and open questions: 
- Should coercion be configurable per-parameter or only per-route? (Initial choice: per-route for simplicity; follow-up epic to add per-param hints).
- How to internationalize user_message? We will expose code and developer_hint; localization responsibility belongs to Console/SDK layers.
- Storage format: compact JSON is small but not canonical; we will canonicalize on save to avoid semantically-equivalent duplicates.

Work breakdown / plan:
- Week 1: finalize compact grammar + spec PR (owner: Liam).
- Week 2: implement fast validator core + unit tests (owner: Backend eng).
- Week 3: hook into serving runtime, telemetry, and Console error rendering (owner: Platform + DX).
- Week 4: catalog migration job + owner notifications (owner: infra).

Review notes / feedback so far: 
- PM (Marcos Ruiz): prefers per-parameter coercion flags for important fields (we will backlog as ENG-453900).
- Security (Priya Gupta): requested explicit guidance for binary blobs and secret parameters — added security review and KMS gating.
- Design (Sophie Tran): wants default user_message to be copy-editable in Console; added field 'user_message_template' to spec.

Open follow-ups (tickets created): [ENG-453900, ENG-453901, ENG-453902] for per-param coercion, localization pipeline, and catalog remediation dashboard.

- [ ] Runtime validator merged and bench <0.2ms p95 added latency
- [ ] Console & SDK render error envelope sensibly
- [ ] Catalog migration job run and owners notified

Notes for future iteration: include richer coercion strategies (date parsing, locale-aware number parsing), and investigate storing a precompiled binary form of compact manifests for even faster load times.
